gates.name: The change adds no secret outside the gitleaks baseline
gates.checks: It scans the commits of the change with the pinned gitleaks rules, and in a local run also the staged files. It fails on a finding that `gitleaks-baseline.json` does not hold, and never on one that the baseline holds. Exit 2 means git or gitleaks is missing in a local run (GitHub Actions exits 1 then), and it never exits 3.
gates.fix: Remove the secret and replace it, or add a finding that is not a secret to `gitleaks-baseline.json` with `Create-GitleaksBaseline.ps1`.

gates.name: Docs cite no source line numbers
gates.checks: It scans the docs for a line number after a file name or after the word line. It does not check that a cited path or symbol exists. Exit 2 means a path passed with `-Path` is missing, and exit 3 means there is no markdown file to scan.
gates.fix: Replace each line number with the file path and the name of the symbol.

gates.name: Artifact links in doc front matter point at files that exist
gates.checks: It reads each doc that sets `story:` in its front matter and checks the story key, the phase and the `relates` paths. It also needs a `because` reason on each `adr` and `spec` edge, and an `intent.assumption` on a discovery or elaboration doc. It skips a doc with no `story:`, and it does not check a URL. Exit 2 means none of the artifact roots exists, and exit 3 means no doc declares a story.
gates.fix: Correct the front matter field that the output names, such as the story key, the phase or a path.

gates.name: Docs have no orphan page, isolated page or broken relative link
gates.checks: It reads every page of the doc layers and fails on a broken relative link, an orphan page or an isolated page. It does not check external links or whether an index is current. Exit 2 means none of the doc layers exists, and exit 3 means the doc layers hold no markdown page.
gates.fix: Link the page from a related page, or correct the broken link so that it points at a file that exists.

gates.name: Each doc index matches what `Build-DocsIndex.ps1` makes from the current pages
gates.checks: It builds each doc index again in memory and compares it with the committed file. It does not check the content or the links of a page. Exit 2 means none of the doc layers exists, and it never exits 3.
gates.fix: Run `Build-DocsIndex.ps1` without `-Check` and commit the index files it writes.

gates.name: Docs hold no em-dash characters
gates.checks: It scans `AGENTS.md` and the doc layers for the em-dash character (U+2014). It also finds the HTML codes that draw it: the named entity mdash, the decimal form 8212 and the hexadecimal form 2014. It does not check source files. Exit 2 means a path passed with `-Path` or the doc layers do not exist, and exit 3 means there is no page to read.
gates.fix: Replace each em-dash with a comma, a colon or a hyphen with a space on each side.

gates.name: The agents file stays within its line and word limit
gates.checks: It counts the lines and the words of the file that `paths.agentsFile` names, and fails over either limit. It does not check what the file says. Exit 2 means the file is missing, and it never exits 3.
gates.fix: Move detail from the agents file into a docs page and link it, until both counts are under the limit.

gates.name: Installed skills, agents and hooks in `.claude/` match the sync manifest, with nothing left over
gates.checks: It compares each file and hook of the installed packages with `sync-manifest.json`, and fails on a missing, changed or stale file. A skill or agent that belongs to the repository itself is left alone. Exit 2 means `apm.yml` or the manifest is missing or git cannot hash a file, and it never exits 3.
gates.fix: Run `apm install` and commit the result, and change a shared file at its source, never in the `.claude/` copy.

gates.name: Every local package in `apm.yml` and `apm.lock.yaml` is a folder that git tracks
gates.checks: It reads each local path in `apm.yml` and `apm.lock.yaml`, and fails on a path that is missing or that git does not track. It does not check a path outside the repository. Exit 2 means `apm.yml` is missing or git cannot answer, and exit 3 means apm.yml and apm.lock.yaml name no local package.
gates.fix: Add the package folder to git, or remove its line from `apm.yml` and its entry from `apm.lock.yaml`.

gates.name: The shared parts of the agents file match the installed packages
gates.checks: It builds the shared parts of the agents file from the installed packages and compares them with the marked parts in the file. It does not check the text outside the markers. Exit 2 means the file, a package part or a marker is missing, and it never exits 3.
gates.fix: Run `Sync-AgentsFile.ps1` without `-Check` and commit the agents file.

gates.name: Docs read at B2 sentences and B1 words
gates.checks: It reads every markdown file and fails on a sentence over 25 words or on a word above level B1. It does not read code, links or the words on the allow list. Exit 2 means a path passed with `-Path` is missing, and exit 3 means there is no markdown file.
gates.fix: Split each long sentence into shorter ones, and replace each hard word with a plain word.

gates.name: Each skill has valid front matter, the standing rules and the failure-mode sections
gates.checks: It reads each skill under `.claude/skills` and checks its name, description, links, standing rules and failure-mode sections. It does not judge whether the text is useful. Exit 3 means there is no skills folder, and it never exits 2.
gates.fix: Add the missing front matter field or section to the skill, as the finding names it.

gates.name: Each agent lists explicit read-only tools, a known persona and the standing rules
gates.checks: It reads each file under `.claude/agents` and checks its name, tools, persona and standing rules. Only the listed writer agent may edit files. Exit 2 means the persona list is missing, and exit 3 means there is no agents folder.
gates.fix: Give the agent an explicit tool list without edit tools, a `Persona:` line from `personas.md` and a standing rules section.

gates.name: Docs name no contributor from the git history
gates.checks: It takes the full names of the commit authors from `git log` and looks for them in `AGENTS.md` and the doc layers. It does not catch a surname alone or a person who never committed. Exit 2 means none of the doc layers exists, and exit 3 means there is no name to check.
gates.fix: Replace the name with the number of the pull request, or add a lawful exception to the person-name allow list.

gates.name: Doc lines and table rows carry a fact, not an empty row or a template leftover
gates.checks: It scans the docs for an empty claim, an empty table row, a template fragment, an empty table and a path from one machine. It does not judge whether a fact is true. Exit 2 means none of the doc roots exists, and exit 3 means the doc roots hold no markdown page.
gates.fix: Delete the empty row or line, or write the fact that it should hold.

gates.name: A change to source also changes its mirrored tests and its docs
gates.checks: It reports a changed source file with no test change in its mirrored test folder, but not a deleted file. It also reports a source area whose docs did not change and that no changed ADR names. A `No-Test` or `No-Docs` commit trailer with a listed reason clears the files of its own commit. Exit 2 means the change could not be listed, and exit 3 means no changed or deleted file carries behaviour.
gates.fix: Add the test and the doc page of the area, or run wrap-up, which writes a `No-Test` or `No-Docs` trailer after the reviewer agrees.

gates.name: The pull request names a story, and its description is not empty or cut off
gates.checks: It looks for a story key such as `#42` in the branch, the title or the description. It also rejects a description that is empty, repeats the title or is too short. It does not check that the story exists. Exit 2 means the pull request text could not be read, and exit 3 means there is no pull request context.
gates.fix: Add the story key to the branch name, the title or the description, and write a description that says what changed and why.

gates.name: A public repository holds no term from the private term list
gates.checks: It checks tracked files, commit messages, the branch name and the pull request text against the private term list. It never prints a term, and it does not check a private repository. Exit 2 means no list was found or a rule is not valid, and exit 3 means the repository is private.
gates.fix: Remove the text at the file and line that the output names, or ask the list owner which rule it breaks.

gates.name: A pointer to a section of another page names a heading that exists
gates.checks: It reads pointers to a named section, a quoted section and a link anchor, and checks that the target page has that heading. It skips a file name that matches more than one file. Exit 3 means there is nothing to scan, and it never exits 2.
gates.fix: Correct the section name or the anchor so that it matches a heading of the target page, or rename the heading.

gates.name: Both doc layers exist, and every unit has a technical page
gates.checks: It checks that each doc layer holds an index and a page, and that each unit has a technical page. The packs or `docs.units` name the units, and a decision record never counts as a page. A missing layer is a finding, so it never exits 2. Exit 3 means no doc layer is set and no unit is named.
gates.fix: Write the page that the output names, or run the adopt-docs skill to draft each missing page.

gates.name: No doc page was last checked longer ago than `docs.lastCheckedMaxAgeDays`
gates.checks: It reads each `Last checked` date in `AGENTS.md` and the doc layers, and lists a date older than `docs.lastCheckedMaxAgeDays`. It does nothing when that setting is off. Exit 3 means the setting is off, and it never exits 2.
gates.fix: Check the facts on the page again and update its `Last checked` date, or raise `docs.lastCheckedMaxAgeDays`.

gates.name: The change adds no commented-out code, open TODO or AI tool name in a C# or Razor comment
gates.checks: It reads only the lines that the change adds to `.cs` and `.razor` files. It fails on commented-out code, on a TODO, FIXME or HACK with no issue key, and on a comment that names an AI tool. Exit 2 means the change could not be worked out, and it never exits 3.
gates.fix: Delete the commented-out code, add an issue key such as `#42` to the TODO, or remove the AI tool name from the comment.

gates.name: The change adds no commented-out code, open TODO or AI tool name in a YAML or PowerShell comment
gates.checks: It reads the comments on the lines that the change adds to PowerShell and YAML files, outside quoted strings, and skips installed files. It reports commented-out code, a TODO, FIXME or HACK with no issue key, and an AI tool name. The help block, `#Requires`, `#region`, a shebang and the marker lines pass. Exit 2 means the change could not be read or a script does not parse, and exit 3 means nothing to check.
gates.fix: Delete the commented-out code, add an issue key such as `#42` to the TODO, or remove the AI tool name from the comment.

gates.name: A native call that the change adds in PowerShell checks its exit code
gates.checks: It parses the added PowerShell lines, and reports a `git`, `az`, `dotnet` or `bicep` call with no exit code check after it. A `||` or `&&` chain and `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true` pass, and it skips installed files. Exit 2 means the change could not be read or a script does not parse, and exit 3 means nothing to check.
gates.fix: Check `$LASTEXITCODE` right after the call and throw when it is not 0, or set `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true` in the script.

gates.name: PSScriptAnalyzer finds nothing on the PowerShell lines that the change adds
gates.checks: It runs PSScriptAnalyzer with its own settings, without the `PSAvoidUsingWriteHost` rule, and reports the findings on the lines that the change adds. It never reads a settings file from the repository, and it skips installed files. Exit 2 means the module is missing or older than 1.21.0, or a script could not be read, and exit 3 means nothing to check.
gates.fix: Change the line as the PSScriptAnalyzer rule asks, or keep a form that `powershell-conventions` asks for and say so in the pull request.

gates.name: The pull request stays within the size limit of the repository
gates.checks: It counts the lines that the change adds and removes since the merge base, and warns above `pullRequest.sizeLimit`. It reads both size settings at the merge base, and skips installed files and the files that `pullRequest.sizeExclude` names. Exit 2 means the change, a setting or a binary file could not be read, and exit 3 means no limit is set.
gates.fix: Split the work into smaller stories with a pull request each, or say in the pull request why it cannot be split.

gates.name: Allow rules of the installed packages are in `.claude/settings.json`
gates.checks: It builds the allow rules from the `allow` lists of the installed packages and fails when one is missing from `.claude/settings.json`. It does not remove a rule, and it does not check the local knowledge folder. Exit 2 means a package list or the settings file cannot be read, and exit 3 means there is no installed package to read.
gates.fix: Run `Sync-AllowRules.ps1` without `-Check` and commit `.claude/settings.json`.
